items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: So I called him up I said, “Max” I said, “we’re doing an album.” And I said, “Would you like to play on a couple of tracks?”

ctx.x: Oh yeah. And you know you get some really fair people and then — and we were lucky enough in my band to find an angel, and this guy, his name was Max Corzilius. Max, when he worked at Dupont he figured out a way to effectively filter jet fuel. He explained it to me one time. But he had the presence of mind at a certain point when he got a little older, he left Dupont and took his patent with him and opened up his own factory to make

this filtered jet fuel, so he became immensely rich, oh my God. So he heard us one time and he said, “Boy I love your band,” he said, “do you guys ever play out here at Smithsonian?” I said, “No, no.” He got us booked at the Smithsonian for their Friday jazz things. And got us booked all over the east coast, Baltimore and a little place called Rock Hall where they had a jazz club. And when we started playing the jazz festival in Clearwater — we’re not there this year but I mean every, for a long time we played…
Yeah, that’s an angel for sure.
